chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, or from Abdillah ibn Amr, and from Rib'i, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah educated Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and perfected his education, so He said: 'Take what is easy and command what is good and turn away from the ignorant.'
And indeed, you are of a great moral character.

When that was the case, He delegated His religion to him, so He said: 'Whatever the Messenger has given you, take it, and whatever he has forbidden you, abstain from it, and fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in retribution.'

So Allah forbade wine itself, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade every intoxicant, and Allah approved that for him. And Allah prescribed the fixed shares (of inheritance), but did not mention the grandfather, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) assigned him a share, and Allah approved that for him. And by Allah, He gives Paradise based on Allah's word, so Allah approves that for him.

key_terms.الْعُرْف: Custom or what is socially acceptable
key_terms.يُعْطِي الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى اللَّهِ: Giving Paradise based on Allah's word/authority

ai.seo_question: How does the Prophet's independent reasoning in Islamic law relate to divine approval according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the theological basis for the Prophet's independent legal reasoning (ijtihad) by citing the verse 'Take what the Messenger gives you' (59:7), demonstrating that his derived rulings carry divine approval. It illustrates this principle through specific examples, such as the prohibition of all intoxicants based on the Quranic ban on wine, and the allocation of a share to the grandfather in inheritance, which was not explicitly detailed in the Quran but was sanctioned by Allah. This underscores the Shia view of the Prophet's authority to legislate within the framework of revelation.
